chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Dawud ibn Sarhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the obligatory recitations (for prostration) are four: 'Recite in the name of your Lord who created' (Al-Alaq), An-Najm, Tanzil al-Sajdah, and Ha-Mim al-Sajdah.

key_terms.اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ: Recite in the name of your Lord (Alaq 1:1)
key_terms.الْعَزَائِم: The obligatory or binding acts (referring to prostrations)

ai.seo_question: What are the four Quranic verses that require prostration upon recitation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), identifying these four 'Azmah' (weighty) verses as obligatory prostrations, a view widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence. This classification highlights the spiritual gravity of these specific revelations, linking the themes of creation, cosmic signs, divine judgment, and guidance to the physical act of submission.
